     3	id: adr-2026-09-16-scenario-evidence-form
     4	title: Evidence of a scenario's effect is the shop's pass/fail where executable, the checking role's mark where not
     5	status: recorded
     6	version: 1
     7	date: 2026-09-16
     8	decided-by: product-authority
     9	right: guardrail
    10	owner: lead-solutions-architect
    11	created: 2026-09-16
    12	updated: 2026-09-16
    13	---
    14	
    15	# ADR: Evidence of a scenario's effect is the shop's pass/fail where executable, the checking role's mark where not
    16	
    17	## 1. Context
    18	
    19	Terms, from the existing type system: a fitness set already carries
    20	`judged` and `executable` as frontmatter fields, one true and the
    21	other false, never both — the
    22	[fitness-set typedef](../basis/artifacts/fitness-set.md) treats a
    23	criterion set an automated runner can execute and a criterion set a
    24	role must read and judge as two distinct, named kinds of check. This
    25	decision applies the same distinction to a feature's scenarios.
    26	
    27	Pre-state, read from lead-shop-held records. `delivery-verified` — the
    28	working principle requiring an implementation's effect "demonstrated
    29	in the running system" before it counted done — was removed whole from
    30	the working set on 2026-09-15
    31	([basis/principles.md](../basis/principles.md) v12, Document History),
    32	under init-delivery-verified-removal, on the product authority's own
    33	words: "There is no mechanism that would be possible to implement in
    34	the current system that would meet the principle. This will need to be
    35	brought back when the system is more mature." The removal deliberately
    36	left open what a check accepts in the principle's place; nothing
    37	replaced it.
    38	
    39	feat-implementation-good (v4), authored against that gap, carries
    40	seven scenarios stating a definition of good for implementation
    41	engineering. Scenario @hash:bbccc3a1765c requires that "the checking
    42	role requires an implementation's effect shown, not declared." At the
    43	feature's add-constraints step the lead-solutions-architect role (this
    44	role) read that scenario against the removal and found no fixed
    45	mechanism naming what evidence a check accepts or which role declares
    46	it satisfied, and recorded that as a needs-decision line rather than
    47	deciding it — feat-implementation-good's Contributors section and its
    48	Edges table row "What form of evidence a check accepts... routed to
    49	adr-authoring." The same feature's own seven scenarios are themselves
    50	an instance of the open question: they are judged reads of definition
    51	documents (this typedef, the role definitions, the fitness set), not
    52	tests any runner can execute — so the question the removal left open
    53	is live in the very feature that raised it.
    54	
    55	The product authority decided this on 2026-09-16 in conversation with
    56	the lead-pm, in two statements, in order:
    57	
    58	1. "Evidence is the shop presenting the pass/fail status of the
    59	   scenario tests."
    60	2. Asked what a pass/fail is for a scenario with no executable test —
    61	   feat-implementation-good's own seven — the authority answered:
    62	   "Scenario tests means executable tests. For non-executable tests,
    63	   the checking role can mark the scenarios as passed."
    64	
    65	Forces. The authority's 2026-09-09 position
    66	([sessions/sess-2026-09-09-c.md](../sessions/sess-2026-09-09-c.md)) —
    67	"the scenario can close when the implementer shows it as complete
    68	through passing scenarios but the PM is ultimately responsible for
    69	whether the delivered feature meets the user need" — sets a level above
    70	this one (the PM's accountability, written into the lead-pm role
    71	definition under init-implementation-process) and is not restated or
    72	contradicted here; this record settles only what a check accepts as
    73	the scenario's own evidence, not what stands above it. The same
    74	session confirmed four defects in `main`'s implementation-role
    75	prompts, one of which bears directly on this decision: "the check held
    76	inside the maker's own prompt." A decision that let a maker's own
    77	declaration stand as evidence, executable or not, would recreate that
    78	defect; the authority's second statement instead names a role other
    79	than the maker — "the checking role" — as the one who marks a
    80	non-executable scenario passed, and feat-implementation-good's own
    81	scenario 4 ("two implementation roles carry the definition, one making
    82	and one checking... neither role is both") already requires that the
    83	checking role and the maker role are not the same role. This decision
    84	does not itself name who fills the checking role; it states only what
    85	counts as evidence once a checking role exists, so it adds no route
    86	back to the defect.
    87	
    88	Options that were real.
    89	
    90	- **One evidence form for every scenario — require every scenario be
    91	  made executable before it can be checked.** Not chosen: the
    92	  authority's own second statement rules it out directly ("for
    93	  non-executable tests, the checking role can mark the scenarios as
    94	  passed") — the authority was asked exactly this question, in the
    95	  concrete case of feat-implementation-good's seven read-based
    96	  scenarios, and declined to force executability as a precondition.
    97	- **The maker's own declaration counts as evidence, for either form.**
    98	  Not chosen: this is the fourth confirmed defect verbatim ("the check
    99	  held inside the maker's own prompt"). The authority's first statement
   100	  requires the shop to present a test's pass/fail status rather than a
   101	  maker's say-so, and the second names the checking role, not the
   102	  maker, as the one who marks a non-executable scenario passed.
   103	
   104	No other option was put to the authority in the recorded conversation;
   105	these two are the ones the two statements, read together, foreclose.
   106	
   107	Self-evaluation against the [adr fitness set](../basis/fitness/adr.fitness.md),
   108	scenario by scenario: (1) the title names the decision in one line and
   109	§2 states it as one sentence a reader can act on, its two forms one
   110	conditional rule rather than two decisions — pass. (2) this Context
   111	states the pre-state and forces with their sources (the removal, the
   112	feature, the two sessions cited) and names two real options with the
   113	reason each was declined — pass. (3) §2 names `decided-by:
   114	product-authority` and `right: guardrail`, standing on the authority's
   115	own word per the typedef's rule — pass. (4) each Consequences bullet
   116	names what changes, for whom, and its cost, and the two bounds on
   117	Bounded Context shops are stated as bounds — pass. (5) §4 states the
   118	decision is hard to reverse once built against, and names its
   119	triggers — pass. (6) §2.1 states the principles screen result,
   120	conformance, against every principle in the set — pass. No fail found
   121	against this fitness set.
   122	
   123	## 2. Decision
   124	
   125	Where a feature's scenario has an executable test, the evidence a
   126	check accepts that the scenario's effect occurred is the shop
   127	presenting that test's pass/fail status; where a scenario has no
   128	executable test, the evidence is the checking role — a role other than
   129	the scenario's maker — marking the scenario passed.
   130	
   131	### 2.1 Principles screen
   132	
   133	Screened against the
   134	[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
   135	conforms, no exception carried.
   136	
   137	- `actor-neutral-discipline` — the rule attaches to the scenario (does
   138	  it carry an executable test or not), never to which kind of actor
   139	  built or checks it; a human checking role and an agent checking role
   140	  mark a non-executable scenario passed under the identical rule, and
   141	  neither gets a lighter bar for being a particular kind of actor.
   142	- `bidirectional-conformance` — this decision states what forward
   143	  conformance evidence a check accepts (did the built scenario do what
   144	  the design said) for the implementation activity generally; it does
   145	  not touch the reverse direction or gate any retirement, so it neither
   146	  conforms further ground it does not need nor conflicts.
   147	- `contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context contract is in
   148	  scope; the decision governs how any shop's own check reads its own
   149	  scenarios, not a channel between two Bounded Contexts.
   150	- `knowable-shape` — no first-class entity (Bounded Context or shop) is
   151	  created or described here; nothing in this decision touches that
   152	  principle's obligation.
   153	- `local-comprehension` — the decision does not change what artifacts
   154	  any level must read; it names what a check accepts as evidence within
   155	  work already scoped to its level.
   156	- `intent-provenance` — the decision does not route intent; it does not
   157	  bear on this principle.
   158	
   159	## 3. Consequences
   160	
   161	- **A shop with an executable scenario test presents that test's
   162	  pass/fail status as its evidence.** What changes: the check no longer
   163	  accepts a maker's declaration that the scenario is done — it requires
   164	  the test's own pass/fail output. For whom: every shop that implements,
   165	  Bounded Context or lead, whose maker role must run and present the
   166	  test; the checking role, who reads the presented status rather than
   167	  taking the maker's word. Cost: an executable scenario cannot close
   168	  without a runnable test existing and being run. Bound on Bounded
   169	  Context shops: a BC shop performing implementation MUST present the
   170	  pass/fail status of a scenario's executable test as that scenario's
   171	  evidence; it MUST NOT substitute its own declaration.
   172	- **A shop with a non-executable scenario has the checking role mark it
   173	  passed.** What changes: where no runner can execute the scenario (a
   174	  judged read of definition documents, as feat-implementation-good's own
   175	  seven scenarios are), the checking role's mark is the evidence, in
   176	  place of a test result that cannot exist. For whom: the checking
   177	  role, who takes on a judgment accountability for these scenarios that
   178	  it did not carry under the removed principle; the maker role, which
   179	  gains no path to mark its own scenario passed. Cost: a non-executable
   180	  scenario's evidence rests on the checking role's judgment rather than
   181	  a reproducible test run, which is weaker evidence than the executable
   182	  form and cannot be independently re-executed later. Bound on Bounded
   183	  Context shops: a BC shop performing implementation MUST route a
   184	  non-executable scenario's pass/fail to a checking role distinct from
   185	  the scenario's maker; it MUST NOT mark its own non-executable
   186	  scenario passed.
   187	- **The maker/checking role split, already required by
   188	  feat-implementation-good's scenario 4 and the working set's
   189	  `define-good-up-front`, is load-bearing for both forms.** What
   190	  changes: nothing new is required of that split by this decision, but
   191	  both evidence forms depend on it — the executable form because the
   192	  checking role, not the maker, is the one reading the presented status
   193	  at check time, and the non-executable form because the mark comes
   194	  from the checking role by name. Cost: none beyond what
   195	  feat-implementation-good already commits to. Forecloses: a
   196	  non-executable scenario closing on the maker's own mark under either
   197	  form.
   198	
   199	Two questions this decision does not settle — the subject named them
   200	neither directly nor by omission the architect can resolve from the
   201	pre-state — are put to the lead-pm role as asks, each with the default
   202	this record acts on for this pass, per the `asks: [lead-pm]` provision
   203	of the `author` step:
   204	
   205	- **Ask 1** (kind: `scope`) — Presented to whom, and where the evidence
   206	  lands. The authority said the shop "presents" the pass/fail status,
   207	  and named no destination. `reconcile-and-close` (the router role's
   208	  process for consuming a BC's completed dispatch) is the obvious
   209	  existing landing point, but feat-implementation-good's own scope note
   210	  says the lead shop's implementation scenarios sit in the lead shop's
   211	  own tree with no dispatch, so `reconcile-and-close` as written may not
   212	  reach them. Default, acted on here: the evidence lands wherever the
   213	  work item that carries the scenario closes — `reconcile-and-close` for
   214	  a dispatched BC scenario, and the equivalent close step of the
   215	  implementation process (not yet defined; session two of
   216	  init-implementation-process) for the lead shop's own. No process
   217	  definition is amended by this record to carry that default; it binds
   218	  only this record's reading until stated in the processes themselves.
   219	- **Ask 2** (kind: `reserved-decision`) — Whether the shop's presented
   220	  pass/fail stands on its own or must be independently re-run by the
   221	  lead. The authority's first statement says the shop "presents" the
   222	  status; it does not say whether presentation alone suffices. Default,
   223	  acted on here: it stands on its own — the authority's word is
   224	  "presenting," not "re-running," and requiring an independent re-run
   225	  is a stronger bar the authority was not asked about and did not
   226	  state; this default may prove wrong and is the lead-pm's to correct.
   227	
   228	## 4. Reversibility
   229	
   230	Hard to reverse once the implementation process (init-implementation-process,
   231	session two) and the maker/checking role definitions are built against
   232	it: both role definitions and the process's check step will be written
   233	to this evidence bar, and every scenario closed under it will have been
   234	closed on this reading of "evidence." Reversing later means rewriting
   235	both role definitions, the process's check step, and re-judging
   236	whatever closed under the old bar. Review triggers: the authority's own
   237	stated intent to bring `delivery-verified` back "when the system is
   238	more mature" — that reinstatement, once it happens, replaces or
